title: Sunfish
slugLine: A browser extension that shields artists’ images from AI training scrapers, wherever they post.

figure.alt: The Sunfish mascot: a round orange sunfish with red spots, drawn in profile.

research.problem: An artist has to ==publish to be hired==, and publishing is also **how the work enters a training set**: the art director browsing and the crawler collecting are served the same image.

painPoints.label: Blocking crawlers
painPoints.detail: It requires running your own site, and it is an honor system the long tail of crawlers ignores.

painPoints.label: Platform settings
painPoints.detail: The control belongs to the platform, not the work. LinkedIn opted its users in by default when it introduced AI training.

painPoints.label: Removal requests
painPoints.detail: They arrive after the fact, once the image has been collected and often already trained on.

painPoints.label: Opt-out registers
painPoints.detail: They depend on the model trainer choosing to check, and on proving afterwards that they did not.

painPoints.label: Going dark
painPoints.detail: Taking work offline means fewer images to license. Commissioned licensing fell 65%, income falls, and the profession gets harder to stay in.

insights.evidence: Portfolio sites, client galleries, shop listings and the feed are where commissions come from, and nothing about a public post tells the art director from the crawler.
Work comes offline, fewer images can be licensed, income falls, and that is an argument for taking more work offline.

insights.insight: Artists will not change how they post
insights.evidence: The persona switches only to a tool that works better than the existing ones and doesn’t change much about his current workflow.

roadmap.what: In development, built by a small team of artists and creatives

Ongoing model tracking to keep protection current as scrapers change

design.lead: Protection that stays with the picture, wherever the picture goes: a browser extension that shields each image on its way out, before it is published.

items.title: Install it once
items.body: Sunfish is a browser extension. There is no separate app to open and no file to prepare before you post.

items.title: Post the way you already do
items.body: It catches each image on its way out, to your portfolio, your feed or your shop, and shields it there.

items.title: Four layers stack on it
items.body: Your followers see the art you made. A scraper has to get through all four.

clauses.label: One protection
clauses.text: is a research problem someone has already published on.

clauses.label: Four, on every image, at scrape scale
clauses.text: is a cost: a decision about whether you are worth it.

columns.label: What it protects, and what it asks of you

rows.label: Glaze
cells: Cloaks your style so mimicry fails. A desktop app you run on each image before posting.

rows.label: Nightshade
cells: Corrupts the training set rather than hiding from it. The same per-image workflow, best applied alongside Glaze.

rows.label: Crawler blocking
cells: Defends a website you control, and does nothing for the same image posted on a platform you don’t.

rows.label: Sunfish
cells: Shields every image you post, wherever you post it, with no step to remember. Installed once, in the browser.

results.lead: Sunfish is in development, with ==a beta targeted for the end of September== and sign-ups open on its landing page.

blocks.title: Until the beta
items: Glaze: free, from the University of Chicago, cloaks your style against mimicry
Nightshade: from the same lab, poisons unauthorised training rather than hiding from it
WebGlaze: a free web version for artists without a machine that can run Glaze
Cloudflare AI controls: block training crawlers at the edge of a portfolio site you run

blocks.title: Said plainly
items: Every tool like this gets attacked eventually. Sunfish is not infallible, but will keep evolving to meet new attacks.
